title: Getting `InputEventMouseMotion` on HTML export on mobile device even though "Emulate Mouse From Touch" is disabled.
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.6.stable.official \[89cea1439\].

### System information

Godot v4.6.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060 SUPER (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9144) - AMD Ryzen 7 3700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 63.92 GiB memory

### Issue description

 When testing an HTML export on my Android device with the Google Chrome browser,
dragging the screen results in `InputEventMouseMotion`, even though the project has `input_devices/pointing/emulate_mouse_from_touch` set to `false`.

When "Emulate Mouse From Touch" is disabled, I expect there to be no mouse inputs while using a mobile device that doesn't have a mouse.

Furthermore, I believe this may be related to another issue where drag events are seemingly incorrect.

Note the following script, where the index of the first touch is being tracked in the variable `_first_touch_index`.

```gdscript
extends Node3D

## Should be `int` or `null`.
var _first_touch_index: Variant = null

func _unhandled_input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
	if event is InputEventMouseButton:
		print("Got mouse button input event.")
	elif event is InputEventMouseMotion:
		print("Got mouse motion input event.")
	elif event is InputEventScreenTouch:
		var screen_touch_event := event as InputEventScreenTouch

		print(
			"Got screen touch input event with index %d." %
			[screen_touch_event.index]
		)

		if screen_touch_event.pressed and _first_touch_index == null:
			_first_touch_index = screen_touch_event.index
			print("Remembered touch index %d." % [screen_touch_event.index])
		elif screen_touch_event.index == _first_touch_index:
			_first_touch_index = null
			print("Forgot touch index %d." % [screen_touch_event.index])
	elif event is InputEventScreenDrag:
		var screen_drag_event := event as InputEventScreenDrag

		print(
			(
				"Got screen drag input event with index %d, " +
				"mouse position %v, drag position %v."
			) % [
				screen_drag_event.index,
				get_viewport().get_mouse_position(),
				screen_drag_event.position
			]
		)

		if screen_drag_event.index == _first_touch_index:
			print(
				(
					"Screen drag with first touch index %d has " +
					"screen relative position %v, " +
					"screen velocity %v."
				) % [
					_first_touch_index,
					screen_drag_event.screen_relative,
					screen_drag_event.screen_velocity
				]
			)

```

First of all, this script demonstrates that `InputEventMouseMotion` occurs on my mobile device when I drag the screen.

Next, if I touch near the bottom left of the screen and drag slightly, I get reasonable results.
```
Got screen drag input event with index 0, mouse position (139.000000, 1970.000000), drag position (139.870117, 1970.770630).
```

```
Screen drag with first touch index 0 has screen relative position (0.999023, 0.000000), screen velocity (71.947235, 0.000000).
```

Note that the script is only printing the screen relative position and screen velocity if the drag event has the same index that is of the first touch. Also, the mouse position is being reported as very near to where the drag position is.

Since it only prints the screen relative position when the drag event corresponds to the first touch index, if I then apply a second touch near the upper right screen and drag the second touch while being careful not to move the first touch, only the drag position prints.

```
Got screen drag input event with index 1, mouse position (954.000000, 101.000000), drag position (954.116333, 101.061722).
```

Again, the mouse position is following the drag position, which is weird to me because there is no mouse involved.

Finally, if I move both the second touch and the first touch slightly, then the relative screen position and screen velocity can become bloated.

```
Screen drag with first touch index 0 has screen relative position (-779.278320, 1732.141724), screen velocity (-1993.570190, 4447.028809).
```

Correct me if I am wrong, but I believe that simultaneous drag events of different touch indexes should not affect each other. I feel like it is related to the mouse input being detected, like as if it thinks the mouse is moving very fast from one touch to the other touch. Maybe I am misunderstanding the input system.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a new project. You don't need Git.

In Project Settings, disable "Emulate Mouse From Touch".

Create a root node with a script that listens for `InputEventMouseMotion`.
```gdscript
func _unhandled_input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
	if event is InputEventMouseMotion:
		print("Got mouse motion input event.")
```

Using Remote Deploy, start an HTTP server.

Open the server's web page on an Android device with the Google Chrome browser.

Use [Google Chrome remote debugging](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/remote-debugging) to see the console logs from the Android device.

Drag the screen of the Android device; it prints `Got mouse motion input event.`.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[minimal-reproducable-project.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25405780/minimal-reproducable-project.zip)
